title: A novel financial performance metric to minimize misclassification costs in model selection
authors: Martin, J.; Abdollahian, M.; Taheri, S.; Akman, D.
tldr: Introduces a financial performance metric (FPM) that estimates true misclassification costs in credit risk, showing traditional cost metrics can underestimate costs by up to 99%, and identifies MLP as the best performer on both statistical and financial criteria.
problem_and_motivation: Standard statistical metrics like AUC, Gini, and Accuracy are widely used for model selection in credit risk but are known to be incoherent for cost-sensitive decisions and may lead to suboptimal commercial outcomes. Existing cost metrics also lack realistic estimates of false prediction costs, particularly regarding exposure at default, lost interest, and remaining months on book.
approach: Simulated four asset classes (Credit Card, Small Loan, Mortgage, LL/SME) using Gamma and Beta distributions to add missing financial variables to the German Credit Dataset.

Proposed a new Financial Performance Metric (FPM) that separately calculates false negative costs (including LGD, EAD, and PV of lost interest) and false positive costs (including opportunity cost and portfolio-level uncertainty).

Compared FPM against the CSEDCM metric and statistical metrics (AUC, Gini, Accuracy) on six ML algorithms: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machine, and Multi-Layer Perceptron.
Evaluated model performance both overall and separately above and below the decision threshold (t=0.5) to expose differential performance.
Validated FPM on a second dataset, the Home Credit Dataset (HCD), with a single portfolio of various product types.
findings: num: CSEDCM underestimated false prediction costs by as much as 99% compared to the proposed FPM (e.g., 1.02% for GBM default cost on CC asset class).
num: MLP showed the lowest overall misclassification costs across all four asset classes (CC: $17.4m, SL: $42.2m, Mo: $260.7m, LL/SME: $488.7m).
RF had the lowest false positive (opportunity) costs, while SVM and MLP performed best on false negative (default) costs for different asset classes.
Statistical metrics (Gini, AUC) produced identical model rankings, confirming redundancy, and Accuracy ranked models differently.
num: On the HCD, FPM identified RF as the best model, yielding a $321.96 million saving over Logistic Regression.
Splitting performance above and below the threshold revealed that model rankings varied greatly, e.g., SVM performed best below threshold on Accuracy but worst above.
Opportunity costs were larger than default costs for larger asset classes, with disparity diminishing as exposure size increased.
key_figures_tables: Table 7: CSEDCM underestimates FPM costs across all models and asset classes by large margins → demonstrates FPM's superior cost sensitivity.
Table 8: FPM costs per $1000 by method, asset class, and threshold → MLP is overall best, RF best for opportunity cost.
Table 9: Statistical metrics (Gini, ACC, AUC) by threshold and method → rankings differ across thresholds and metrics.
Table 10: HCD results show FPM identifies RF as best, saving $322M over LR → confirms FPM robustness.
Figure 1: Power curve for GCD shows >95% power at sample size 655 → validates sample adequacy.

key_equations.explanation: Total misclassification cost as sum of false negative and false positive costs.

key_equations.equation: FNC = \sum_{i=1}^{N} P(\hat{y}_i < t | y_i = 1) \times LGD \times EAD + PV(ROI \times RMOB)
key_equations.explanation: Cost of misclassifying a defaulter as good, including LGD, EAD, and lost interest.

key_equations.equation: FPC = \sum_{i=1}^{N} P(\hat{y}_i > t | y_i = 0) \times PV(ROI) - (ROI + \bar{y} \times EAD \times LGD)
key_equations.explanation: Cost of misclassifying a good applicant as bad, including opportunity cost and portfolio-level expected loss.
Area under ROC curve, a common but criticized statistical metric.

definitions.definition: Financial Performance Metric; proposed cost metric that sums false negative and false positive costs with realistic components.
Credit Scoring Example Dependent Cost Matrix; a prior cost metric by Bahnsen et al. that the authors find underestimates costs.
Exposure at Default; the actual amount a lender has at risk at the time of default.
Loss Given Default; the fraction of EAD lost in the event of default.
Remaining Months On Book; months remaining on a loan's repayment term, used to calculate lost interest.
Multi-Layer Perceptron; an artificial neural network with multiple hidden layers, used in credit scoring.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper makes a significant contribution to credit risk modeling by proposing a novel Financial Performance Metric (FPM) that provides a more realistic and accurate estimate of misclassification costs compared to existing metrics. It systematically demonstrates the inadequacy of commonly used statistical metrics (AUC, Gini, Accuracy) and even prior cost metrics (CSEDCM) for model selection in commercial settings. By evaluating a range of machine learning algorithms on both statistical and financial criteria, it provides a benchmark for future work and highlights the importance of evaluating performance separately on either side of the decision threshold. The paper also contributes a methodology for augmenting public datasets with simulated financial variables to enable cost-based comparisons.
directly_justifies: CSEDCM underestimates false prediction costs by as much as 99% compared to FPM.
MLP outperformed other methods on statistical metrics and overall on financial costs.
A mix of algorithms worked best on either side of the decision threshold.
The proposed FPM would provide a significant financial benefit to organisations.
limits: Relies on simulated financial variables rather than real-world data, which may not fully capture real portfolio dynamics.
The GCD has a default rate (~30%) much higher than typical industry portfolios, limiting generalizability.
Only six algorithms were compared, and hyperparameter tuning was minimal to avoid overfitting.
Credit card asset class was modeled as a one-off loan, not as a revolving credit line.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. The paper is highly relevant to domains 6 (Predictive Modeling) and 12 (Evaluation Frameworks) because it directly proposes and compares predictive models and a new evaluation metric. It has medium relevance to 14.A (Synthetic Data) due to the extensive simulation of financial variables. It has contextual relevance to 7 (Budgeting) because the cost-sensitive optimization paradigm is analogous, but the paper does not address budget allocation or recommendation. Topics 1-5, 9-11, and 13 were considered and rejected as they focus on demographics, cultural practices, UX design, user engagement, and specific financial goals, none of which are covered. The overall topical coverage is centered on algorithmic evaluation and cost-sensitive learning in credit risk.

limitations: Relies on simulated variables (EAD, LGD) rather than real portfolio data, which may not capture true cost dynamics [unacknowledged].
Credit card asset class was simulated as a term loan, not as a revolving credit line, potentially underestimating interest revenue [unacknowledged].
The GCD has a default rate (~30%) far higher than typical real-world portfolios, which may affect model performance and cost estimates [unacknowledged].
Model tuning was minimal to avoid overfitting, but this may not have optimized each algorithm's potential [acknowledged].
Only individual algorithms were tested; a stacking or ensemble approach across the threshold is proposed but not evaluated [acknowledged].
remember_this: CSEDCM underestimates credit misclassification costs by up to 99% compared to the proposed FPM.
MLP achieved the lowest overall financial cost across all four simulated asset classes.
Model rankings differ dramatically when evaluated above versus below the decision threshold.
Opportunity costs dominate for larger loans, while default costs are relatively more important for smaller loans.
The proposed FPM would provide a significant financial benefit to organisations in model selection.
